question: Which country has recently passed a landmark law legally recognising femicide and making it punishable with life imprisonment?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Italy.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__** 

__
 
• **Italy** has passed a historic law recognising **femicide**—the gender-motivated killing of women—as a separate crime punishable with **life imprisonment**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

__
 
• The law formally defines **femicide** as the intentional killing of women due to their gender, often rooted in misogyny and patriarchal control.
 
• Italy classifies femicide under **three categories**: partner-related, family-related, and non-family perpetrators.
 
• Recognising femicide separately helps generate **accurate national statistics** for targeted policymaking.
 
• The legislation aims to strengthen understanding of **gendered violence, toxic masculinity** and patterns preceding gender-based killings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

__
 
• **Meaning of Femicide**__

 __
 
• Defined as the killing of women precisely because they are women.
 
• 
 
• 
 
 
 
• **Why Recognition Matters**__
 __
 
• Identifies gendered motives behind severe violence against women.
 
• Helps law enforcement track patterns of harassment, coercion and escalation.
 
• Aids in shaping prevention strategies and victim protection systems.
 
 
 
• **Categories Recognised Under the Law**__
 __
 
• **Partner-related** femicide (most common globally).
 
• **Family-related** femicide involving household or relatives.
 
• **Non-family perpetrators** including acquaintances or strangers.
 
 
 
• **Social Significance**__
 
 
• Promotes awareness of **misogyny, harassment and control-driven violence**.
 
• Highlights need for early interventions and counselling for at-risk individuals.
